objective: By the end of this lesson you can plan a taxi route, get and read back a taxi clearance, read airport signs, markings and lights, hold the controls for the wind, and taxi safely to the runway without a runway incursion.
why: A runway incursion can happen on any taxi, and about three occur each day at U.S. towered airports [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]]. It only takes one missed instruction or turn to cause an accident [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

prereading.what: Taxiing: situational awareness, speed, brake check, steering, wind control positions, taxi checks.
prereading.label: AFH Ch 2, 2-18 to 2-21

prereading.what: Single-pilot taxi planning, written taxi instructions, radio calls, runway crossings, exterior lights.
prereading.label: AC 91-73B, pages 3-10

prereading.what: Marking colors, taxiway and holding position markings, mandatory, location and direction signs.
prereading.label: AIM 2-3-1 to 2-3-10

prereading.what: Taxi clearances, required readbacks, progressive taxi, taxi in low visibility.
prereading.label: AIM 4-3-18 to 4-3-19

prereading.printed: PHAK Appendix C, C-1 to C-4
prereading.what: Color charts of standard airport signs and markings.
prereading.label: PHAK Appendix C, C-1 to C-4

warmup: Ground says: "Cessna 345, Runway 27, taxi via Alpha, hold short of Runway 18." Are you allowed to cross Runway 18? Are you allowed to taxi onto Runway 27?

key_terms.def: Runways, taxiways and other areas used for taxi, takeoff and landing, not including ramps and parking areas. At a towered airport you need ATC approval to enter it [[34:381|AIM P/CG]].
A place on the airport movement area with a history or risk of collisions or runway incursions, where extra attention is needed [[34:358|AIM P/CG]].

Any event in the runway environment involving an aircraft, vehicle, person or object on the ground that creates a collision hazard or loss of separation with an aircraft taking off or landing [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]].
Four yellow lines across the taxiway, two solid and two dashed; the solid lines are on the side where you must hold [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a]].
Red sign with white letters marking a runway or critical-area entrance, or an area you may not enter [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8]].
Step-by-step taxi directions from ATC, available when you are unsure of the route [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b3]].
A wrong picture that persists even when the evidence says otherwise; often hits pilots who expect their usual taxi route [[30:45|RMH 6-2]] [[30:46|RMH 6-3]].
The tendency of the airplane to turn into the wind while on the ground, which makes crosswind steering harder [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

chunks.title: Plan the taxi before you move

body.p: Taxi planning is part of flight planning, done just like the other phases of flight [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b]]. Use current airport information, not memory.

head: Resource
What it tells you for taxi
rows: The most complete information on a public airport; includes airport diagrams for selected towered airports and LAHSO data [[1:337|PHAK 14-3]] [[1:338|PHAK 14-4]]
Runways, taxiways and hot spots. Keep it out and in view the whole taxi [[24:55|AFH 2-18]]
Time-critical, temporary items such as runway and taxiway closures and construction [[1:338|PHAK 14-4]] [[1:339|PHAK 14-5]]
Weather, runways in use and construction that could affect taxi planning [[1:339|PHAK 14-5]]

body.p: Hot spots are shown on airport diagrams as a brown open circle or ellipse with a number such as HS 1; the number matches a written description [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide, Hot Spots]].

bullets: Before taxi: review the diagram and hot spots for the big picture [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)(d)]].
Brief the expected route, hold short lines, runways to cross and hot spots [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]].
Finish as many checklist items as you can (flaps, trim, GPS entries) before you start moving [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(g)]].
If ATC clears you onto a runway or taxiway that the NOTAM or ATIS says is closed, ask the controller to verify [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)(c)]].

callout.text: A closed runway may not have a visible yellow X, depending on why and how long it is closed. Check NOTAMs and ATIS [[33:161|AIM 2-3-6e]].

check.q: Where do you find out about a taxiway closed for construction today?

body.p: At a towered airport you need approval before moving onto the movement area, and you always state where you are on the airport when you call [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a]]. On first contact say who you are, where you are, what you want and what you know, for example: "Cessna N1234, at SeaBreeze FBO, VFR to taxi, with information Alpha" [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(2)]].

bullets: A clearance is required to cross ANY runway. ATC gives an explicit clearance for every crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].
Being assigned a takeoff runway does NOT let you enter or cross that runway at any point [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]].
ATC does not use the word "cleared" for taxi, to avoid confusion [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]].

head: Always read back
Source
rows: Any clearance to enter a specific runway
Any hold short or line up and wait instruction

body.p: Example: Ground: "Beechcraft 13159, runway two seven, taxi via taxiways Charlie and Delta, hold short of runway three three left." Pilot: "Beechcraft 13159, runway two seven, hold short of runway three three left" [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18d1]]. Use your full call sign and the runway; do not answer with just "Roger" or "Wilco" [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

callout.text: Write it down. "Taxi 9R via B, E, J, hold short 4L at E" becomes "9R B E J 4L E" with the hold short limit circled [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e(2)]]. Not sure of the route? Ask for progressive taxi [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b3]].

body.p: Nontowered airports: self-announce on the CTAF before taxiing and before taxiing onto the runway for departure [[33:207|AIM TBL 4-1-1]]. Example: "Strawn traffic, Queen Air 7155B (location on airport) taxiing to runway two six, Strawn" [[33:210|AIM 4-1-9g]]. Monitor CTAF from engine start, and remember some aircraft have no radio [[7:14|AC 91-73B App 1]].
No radio at a towered airport? You need a light signal before taxiing on a runway and before takeoff or landing [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18c]]. A flashing green means cleared to taxi [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]].

check.q: Ground says "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha, hold short of Runway 18." What must your readback include?
check.a: Your call sign, Runway 27, and "hold short of Runway 18" [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

head: Sign
Colors
Meaning
rows: Mandatory (runway holding position, ILS, No Entry)
Runway or critical-area entrance, or no entry [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8]]
The taxiway or runway you are ON [[33:165|AIM 2-3-9]]
Taxiways leading out of the intersection [[33:167|AIM 2-3-10]]
Way to places like runways, terminals, cargo [[1:350|PHAK 14-16]]
Shows when you are clear of the runway or ILS critical area [[33:166|AIM 2-3-9a3]]
Runway left in thousands of feet [[1:350|PHAK 14-16]]

body.p: A holding position sign such as "15-33" means the Runway 15 threshold is to your left and Runway 33 is to your right [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]]. Treat it like an airport stop sign [[1:341|PHAK 14-7]].

Direction signs are normally on the left before the intersection. The taxiways are listed clockwise starting from the first one on your left. If a location sign is in the array, left turns are on its left and straight-ahead or right turns are on its right [[33:167|AIM 2-3-10]].

callout.text: Black box = where you ARE. Yellow box = where you can GO. Red box = STOP until cleared.

check.q: You see a yellow "B" on a black square. What does it tell you?
check.a: You are on Taxiway B; it is a taxiway location sign [[33:165|AIM 2-3-9a1]].

body.p: Runway markings are white. Taxiway markings, closed or hazardous areas and holding positions (even on a runway) are yellow [[33:138|AIM 2-3-2b]]. Runways have white segmented centerlines; taxiways have continuous yellow centerlines [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]].

bullets: Taxiway centerline: one continuous yellow line. Keep the airplane centered on it, but that does not guarantee wingtip clearance [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b1]].
Enhanced centerline: yellow dashes on both sides of the centerline, up to 150 feet before a runway holding position. Get ready to stop [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].
Solid double yellow edge lines: pavement beyond is not for aircraft. Dashed double yellow: the next pavement is usable, like a ramp [[33:145|AIM 2-3-4c]].
Single dashed yellow line across a taxiway: taxiway/taxiway holding position [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5c]] [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5c]].
Surface painted signs: red with white letters for holding positions, black with yellow for location [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5d]] [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4f]].

head: Light
Color
Meaning
rows: You are in the runway environment or ILS critical area [[1:352|PHAK 14-18]]
Flashing yellow (pair beside taxiway or in-pavement row)
Taxiway/runway intersection, at the runway holding position [[1:353|PHAK 14-19]]
Confirms clearance to enter or cross in low visibility [[1:353|PHAK 14-19]]
Unsafe to enter, cross or take off. They never give a clearance [[1:353|PHAK 14-19]]

head: Light gun (aircraft on the ground)
Meaning
rows: Taxi clear of the runway in use [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]]
Return to starting point on airport [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]]

body.p: In daylight, acknowledge tower light signals by moving the ailerons or rudder; at night, blink the landing or navigation lights [[33:257|AIM 4-3-13e]].

check.q: You see yellow dashes on both sides of the taxiway centerline. What is ahead?
check.a: A runway holding position marking, within 150 feet. Prepare to stop unless cleared [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].

chunks.title: Hold lines: entering and crossing runways

body.p: When told "hold short of Runway XX", stop so that no part of the airplane is past the holding position marking [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]]. Stop before the solid lines so no part of the airplane touches the first solid yellow line [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]]. Crossing a hold line without clearance can lead to a Pilot Deviation [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

head: Situation
What you do
rows: Do not cross the hold line without an ATC clearance [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]]
Cross only when the runway is clear and nobody is on final; look both ways [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]]

No clearance needed to cross this marking; you are clear only when the WHOLE airplane, tail too, is past both dashed and solid lines [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]] [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(11)]]. Never exit onto another runway without ATC clearance [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(6)]]
Stop at the ILS marking when told; do not cross without clearance [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5b]]

bullets: Before entering or crossing, be POSITIVE ATC cleared you. Scan the whole runway and the final approach [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(4)]].
Bring the airplane to a full stop at the runway entrance before doing checklists [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(5)]].
At a nontowered field, listen on CTAF and scan the final approach and departure paths of the runway [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(12)]].
When cleared to cross, do it promptly [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(6)]].

callout.text: Lost or unsure? Never stop on a runway. Stop clear of it, tell ATC, and ask for progressive taxi [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]] [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(7)]].

check.q: After landing you stop with your main wheels past the hold line but your tail still over the dashed lines. Are you clear of the runway?
check.a: No. All parts of the airplane must be past the holding position marking [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]] [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7d(11)]].

chunks.title: Wind: read it, then hold the controls for it

body.p: Check the wind indicators even when CTAF gives you wind, because that information may not be accurate [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].

bullets: Wind sock: shows direction and lets you estimate speed and gusts. It stands straighter in strong wind and swings back and forth in gusts [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].
Wind tee and tetrahedron: can swing with the wind, but can also be set by hand to the runway in use, so check the wind sock too [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].
Tetrahedron: the small end points in the direction of landing [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].

head: Wind from
Ailerons
Elevator (nosewheel airplane)
rows: Upwind aileron UP (yoke toward the wind)
Upwind aileron DOWN (yoke away from the wind)
Neutral; ailerons are not for steering

body.p: Why: a headwind wants to lift the upwind wing; the up aileron spoils that lift. A tailwind wants to get under the tail and wing and nose the airplane over; down elevator and down upwind aileron stop that [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

callout.text: Headwind: yoke INTO it. Tailwind: yoke AWAY and forward. Check the wind again after every turn, because a turn changes which corner it hits.

check.q: Wind is from your left rear. Where do the controls go?
check.a: Yoke forward (elevator down) and turned right, so the left (upwind) aileron is down [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

bullets: 1. Get ATIS, then the clearance or CTAF call. Read back, write it down, and trace the route on the airport diagram [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7g(1)]].
2. Lights on per the next chunk; check the area clear of people, equipment and aircraft [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)]] [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
3. Add a little power to start rolling, then pull the throttle back right away so you do not speed up too much [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
4. Brake check right away: throttle back, press one brake, then the other. If braking is bad, shut down the engine at once [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
5. Speed: slow enough that closing the throttle stops you promptly. Throttle at idle before using brakes, except in sharp, slow turns [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
6. Steer with rudder pedals; add brake only to tighten a turn after full pedal. Slow down before turning [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
7. Keep the yellow centerline under the middle of the fuselage. Eyes outside, side to side, near and far [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
8. Hold controls for the wind and fix them after each turn [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

9. On the way, check instruments: airspeed near zero, attitude level, altimeter at field elevation, turn needle the right way with ball to the outside, heading indicator set to the compass, VSI zero [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
10. Stop short of the hold line, nosewheel straight, and do the run-up checklist [[24:57|AFH 2-20]] [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

head: Checkride standard
What it means in practice
rows: ACS PA.II.D.S1: Receive and correctly read back clearances/instructions, if applicable
Runway, hold short and crossing items word for word, with call sign
ACS PA.II.D.S2: Use an airport diagram or taxi chart during taxi, if published, and maintain situational awareness
Diagram out, know where you are and what is next
ACS PA.II.D.S3: Position the flight controls for the existing wind, if applicable
Correct aileron and elevator for each leg of the route
ACS PA.II.D.S4: Complete the appropriate checklist(s)
POH taxi items and instrument checks
ACS PA.II.D.S5: Perform a brake check immediately after the airplane begins moving
Test brakes in the first few feet
ACS PA.II.D.S6: Maintain positive control ... without excessive use of brakes
Control speed with the throttle, not by riding the brakes
ACS PA.II.D.S7: Comply with airport/taxiway markings, signals, and ATC clearances and instructions
Follow signs, lines, light signals and the clearance actually given
ACS PA.II.D.S8: Position the airplane properly relative to hold lines
No part of the airplane past the hold line

check.q: When do you test the brakes?
check.a: As soon as the airplane starts moving [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] (ACS PA.II.D.S5).

head: When
Lights
rows: Navigation/position and anti-collision lights on. Taxi light on when moving, off when stopped or yielding. No strobes if they blind others [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24e]]
Entering the departure runway or line up and wait
Takeoff clearance, or starting the roll at a nontowered field

callout.text: 14 CFR 91.209: from sunset to sunrise you may not operate an aircraft without lighted position lights. Day or night, an installed anticollision light system must be on, unless the PIC decides that turning it off is safer because of operating conditions [[60:491|14 CFR 91.209]].

body.p: Night: check the ramp with a flashlight before getting in, clear the propeller area carefully, taxi slowly, and follow painted taxi lines. Do not blind other pilots with your lights. The airplane can creep forward unnoticed during the run-up, so hold the brakes [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].

Low visibility raises the risk of a runway incursion. Use everything: airport diagram, heading indicator, signs, markings and lights, and do all heads-down work while stopped [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(4)]]. Hold checklists and nonessential talk until stopped with brakes set [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19d]]. Tell the controller at the first sign of becoming disoriented, and use extra caution taxiing toward the sun [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19b]].
Below 1,200 feet RVR, some airports use special low-visibility taxi routes with geographic position markings (a pink circle with a number) and stop bars [[33:149|AIM 2-3-4g]] [[1:353|PHAK 14-19]].

check.q: You are about to cross a runway at night. Which exterior lights?
check.a: All exterior lights, considering their effect on others [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24f]] [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(c)]].

chunks.title: Risk: distractions, bias, route changes, incursions

head: Hazard
How a good pilot handles it
rows: Do checklists only when stopped or taxiing straight with no complex intersections. Keep a sterile cockpit, phones off, and limit instruction while taxiing [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(a)]] [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(j)]] [[7:17|AC 91-73B App 3]]

Pilots who get the same clearance every day start hearing what they expect [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[30:46|RMH 6-3]]. Follow the clearance you actually received, not the one you expected [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(e) CAUTION]]

Stop if needed, write down the new route, read it back and re-trace it on the diagram. Any change must be fully understood [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]]. If anything conflicts, do not continue the taxi [[24:225|AFH 11-8]]
Read back hold shorts, know the signs, check NOTAMs, ask for progressive taxi, and check for traffic before every hold line [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]]

bullets: Similar call sign on frequency? Be extra careful not to take their clearance [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(6)]].
Many incursions happen even after a correct hold-short readback. Use a reminder, such as something hung on the yoke [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(3)]].
Tired? Fatigue makes expectation and confirmation bias more likely [[30:46|RMH 6-3]].

check.q: Ground gives you a different route than usual and you only half heard it. What should you do?
check.a: Ask ATC to clarify before moving; the PIC should get clarification of any instruction not understood [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f]].

bullets: Taxiing with so much power that speed has to be controlled with the brakes [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
Riding the brakes downwind instead of using minimum power and only occasional braking [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
Fast, sharp turns: side loads, tire damage or a swerve, especially turning from downwind to upwind [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Using ailerons to steer, or forgetting to change the control position after a turn [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].
Skipping the brake check, or not checking flight instruments while taxiing [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
Head down in the cockpit, losing track of position or the next turn [[7:5|AC 91-73B 7d]].
Stopping with part of the airplane over the hold line, or stopping with the nosewheel turned [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].
Doing the run-up on loose gravel or with the tail toward something the prop blast could damage [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].

check.q: Your speed keeps creeping up and you keep tapping the brakes. What is wrong?
check.a: Too much power. Reduce the throttle so speed depends on the throttle, and close it before braking [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

scenario.title: The usual route, but not today
scenario.setup: You fly from your home towered airport every week and always get "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha." Today ATIS mentions construction on Alpha. You have a friend in the right seat chatting about the flight, and your tablet is still loading the route. Ground says: "Cessna 345, Runway 27, taxi via Bravo, cross Runway 18, hold short of Runway 27 at Bravo 3." A Piper with call sign 354 is also on frequency.

questions.q: What bias is most likely to trap you here, and what is your defense?
questions.a: Expectation bias: hearing "via Alpha" because that is normal [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[30:46|RMH 6-3]]. Write the clearance down, read it back, and trace Bravo on the diagram [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]].
Call sign, Runway 27, the Runway 18 crossing, and hold short of Runway 27 at Bravo 3 [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

questions.q: How do you handle your passenger and the tablet?
questions.a: Finish the tablet setup before moving and ask for a sterile cockpit, but invite them to speak up if they see a conflict [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(b), (g)]] [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(3) NOTE]].

questions.q: Halfway there you hear "345, cross Runway 18" but are not sure it was for you. What now?
questions.a: With a similar call sign on frequency, do not act on a clearance that may be for the other aircraft. Hold short and ask ATC [[7:6|AC 91-73B 7d(6)]] [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18b1]].

questions.q: Ground changes your route to Charlie. What do you do?
questions.a: Stop if needed, write it down, read it back, re-trace it on the diagram, and keep checking for hot spots [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(d)]]. If anything conflicts, do not continue [[24:225|AFH 11-8]].

skills.do: Call for taxi, receive the clearance and read back runway, crossings and hold shorts correctly.
skills.practice: Listen to ground frequency recordings or chair-fly with a friend acting as ground; write clearances in shorthand [[7:7|AC 91-73B 7e]].

skills.do: Follow your position on the airport diagram and know the next turn and hot spot.
skills.practice: Before each lesson, trace the likely route and hot spots on the current diagram [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7g(1)]].

skills.do: Hold the right aileron and elevator for the wind on every leg of the route.
skills.practice: Say the wind corner and control position out loud after each turn [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

skills.do: Complete POH taxi items and instrument checks while taxiing.
skills.practice: Do the instrument check on a straight, quiet stretch of taxiway [[24:58|AFH 2-21]] [[7:4|AC 91-73B 7b(2)(a)]].

skills.do: Test both brakes as soon as the airplane starts moving.
skills.practice: Make it a habit on every taxi: roll, throttle back, left brake, right brake [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

skills.do: Control speed and direction with throttle and rudder, using brakes sparingly.
skills.practice: Practice taxiing with idle or near-idle power and small throttle changes [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

skills.do: Follow signs, markings, light signals and ATC instructions exactly.
skills.practice: Name each sign and marking out loud as you pass it.

skills.do: Stop with no part of the airplane past the hold line.
skills.practice: Have your instructor confirm your stopping point from outside or by looking over the nose [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a1]].

quiz.q: A red sign with white "15-33" on a taxiway means:
options: You are on Runway 15-33
Runway holding position: Runway 15 threshold to the left, 33 to the right
Runway 15-33 is closed
Direction to Runway 15-33
quiz.why: It is a runway holding position sign; the numbers match the thresholds' directions [[33:162|AIM 2-3-8b1]].

quiz.q: Ground says "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha." Alpha crosses Runway 36. May you cross Runway 36?
options: Yes, a runway assignment includes all crossings
Yes, if no one is on final
No, ATC must issue an explicit clearance for every runway crossing
Only if you read back the clearance
quiz.why: A clearance is required before crossing any runway, and ATC issues an explicit clearance for all crossings [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].

quiz.q: Taxiing with a quartering headwind from the left, you should hold:
options: Left aileron up, elevator neutral
Left aileron down, elevator down
Right aileron up, elevator up
Neutral ailerons, elevator down
quiz.why: Upwind aileron up and neutral elevator for a nosewheel airplane in a quartering headwind [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

quiz.q: Taxiing with a quartering tailwind from the right, you should hold:
options: Right aileron up, elevator neutral
Right aileron down, elevator down
Left aileron down, elevator up
Neutral ailerons, elevator up
quiz.why: Quartering tailwind: elevator down and upwind aileron down [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

quiz.q: Yellow dashes on both sides of the taxiway centerline warn you:
options: The taxiway ends ahead
You are entering a non-movement area
A runway holding position is ahead, within 150 feet
The pavement is not strong enough
quiz.why: The enhanced taxiway centerline runs up to 150 feet before a runway holding position marking [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b2]].

quiz.q: A flashing green light from the tower to an airplane on the ground means:
options: Cleared for takeoff
Cleared for taxi
Return to starting point
Exercise extreme caution
quiz.why: Flashing green to an aircraft on the ground means cleared for taxi [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]].

quiz.q: The right way to control taxi speed is to:
options: Set cruise power and use the brakes
Ride the brakes lightly the whole time
Use enough power that closing the throttle stops the airplane promptly, with throttle at idle before braking
Use full flaps for drag
quiz.why: Speed should depend on the throttle; taxiing with power that needs braking is a common error [[24:56|AFH 2-19]] [[24:57|AFH 2-20]].

quiz.q: You become unsure of your position while taxiing at a towered airport. You should:
options: Stop on the nearest runway and look around
Keep going and look for a sign
Stop clear of any runway, tell ATC, and ask for progressive taxi
Turn around and go back to parking
quiz.why: Never stop on a runway; stop, advise ATC, and request progressive taxi if needed [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(5)]].

takeaways: Plan the taxi: current diagram, NOTAMs, ATIS and hot spots before you move.
Read back runway, crossings and hold shorts with your call sign, and write complex clearances down.
Red sign = stop until cleared; black = where you are; yellow = where to go.
No part of the airplane past the hold line unless cleared; when exiting, the whole airplane must be past it.
Headwind: yoke toward the wind. Tailwind: yoke away from the wind and forward.
Control speed with the throttle, test brakes right away, and keep your eyes outside.
cfi_notes: AC 91-73B recommends instructors limit cockpit instruction during taxiing [[7:17|AC 91-73B App 3]]. Do the teaching in the briefing before engine start and the debrief after.
Students often say "Roger" to hold-short instructions. Make them read back the runway and "hold short" every time [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].
Have students name the wind quadrant at each turn; many forget to change the control position after turning.
Examiners often give a route change mid-taxi or a crossing at a hot spot to test R2/R3; practice this at your home field.
Make students check NOTAMs for taxiway closures; AC 91-73B and the NTSB-style bias examples in RMH Ch 6 make good discussion [[30:45|RMH 6-2]].
Demonstrate how close a wingtip can be even when centered on the line: centerline does not guarantee wingtip clearance [[33:144|AIM 2-3-4b1]].
gaps: Airplane-specific taxi checklist, steering limits, brake system and light limits come from the POH/AFM, which is not in the resources.
Specific Chart Supplement legend decoding and the current hot spot list for a given airport are not in these files; use the current Chart Supplement and Terminal Procedures.
AC 120-57 (low visibility SMGCS taxi charts) is referenced by AIM 4-3-19 but not included.
Tailwheel taxi technique is covered in AFH Ch 14 but not taught here (lesson is for nosewheel ASEL).

activities.title: Which kind of sign is it?
activities.intro: Tap a clue, then tap the sign type it belongs to.
buckets: Direction or destination: black on yellow

items.t: "15-33" beside a taxiway where it meets a runway
"ILS" where you hold short of the ILS critical area
A sign telling you an aircraft may not enter this area
"B" naming the taxiway you are on right now
A runway number telling you which runway you are on
Taxiway letters with arrows for the turns out of an intersection
An arrow pointing the way to the terminal or cargo area

activities.title: True or false: clearances and hold lines

cards.s: Ground says "Runway 27, taxi via Alpha." You may cross any runway on the way.
cards.why: No. You need a clearance to cross any runway, and ATC gives an explicit clearance for every crossing [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a5]].

cards.s: Being assigned Runway 27 lets you taxi onto Runway 27 when you get there.
cards.why: No. A runway assignment does not let you enter or cross that runway at any point [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a6]].

cards.s: "Roger" is a good enough answer to a hold-short instruction.
cards.why: No. Read back your full call sign, the runway and "hold short". Avoid "Roger" or "Wilco" here [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

cards.s: On a runway hold line, the solid yellow lines are on the side where you must stop.
cards.why: Yes. The solid lines are always on the side where the aircraft must hold [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a]].

cards.s: After landing, you need an ATC clearance to cross the hold line as you exit the runway.
cards.why: No. No clearance is needed to cross it when exiting. You are clear only when the whole airplane is past both the dashed and solid lines [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

cards.s: At a nontowered airport, you may cross a runway hold line once the runway is clear and nobody is on final.
cards.why: Yes. Then cross with extreme caution and look both ways [[1:342|PHAK 14-8]].

activities.title: Set the yoke for the wind
activities.intro: Tap a wind, then where the yoke goes.

pairs.r: Yoke turned right and pushed forward
Yoke turned left and pushed forward

activities.title: From parking to run-up: put it in order
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Call ground: who, where, what you want, and the ATIS code
Read back the clearance, write it down and trace it on the diagram
Add a little power to start rolling, then pull the throttle back
Test the brakes: one side, then the other
Taxi on the centerline with the controls set for the wind, checking instruments
Stop at the run-up spot, clear of the taxiway, nosewheel straight
Do the before-takeoff checklist from the POH

final_quiz.q: You read a NOTAM that says Taxiway Charlie is closed today. Ground then says: "Cessna 8JP, Runway 24, taxi via Charlie." What should you do?
options: Taxi via Charlie, because ATC always knows the airport status
Pick another taxiway that looks open and tell ATC later
Ask the controller to verify the clearance before you taxi
Wait on the ramp until the NOTAM expires
final_quiz.why: If ATC clears you onto a taxiway that a NOTAM or ATIS says is closed, ask the controller to verify the clearance [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)(c)]]. At a towered airport you need approval to move on the movement area, so never pick your own route [[33:260|AIM 4-3-18a]].

final_quiz.q: You are planning your taxi at a busy airport. How is a hot spot shown on the airport diagram?
options: A brown open circle or ellipse with a label like HS 2
A red X over the taxiway
A yellow box with the word CAUTION
A dashed blue line around the area
final_quiz.why: Hot spots are a brown open circle or ellipse with a number such as HS 1. The number matches a written description [[2:124|Chart Users' Guide, Hot Spots]]. Review them before you taxi [[7:3|AC 91-73B 7b(1)(d)]].

final_quiz.q: Ground says: "Cessna 52T, Runway 31, taxi via Delta, cross Runway 4, hold short of Runway 9." Which readback is best?
options: "Roger, 52T."
"Runway 31, cross 4, hold short of 9."
"Cessna 52T, taxi via Delta, wilco."
"Cessna 52T, Runway 31, cross Runway 4, hold short of Runway 9."
final_quiz.why: Read back the runway assignment, runway crossings and hold shorts [[33:261|AIM 4-3-18a9]] [[1:365|PHAK 14-31]]. Include your full call sign, and don't use "Roger" or "Wilco" for these [[7:8|AC 91-73B 7f(4)]].

final_quiz.q: Look at panel (c) of the figure. You are on Taxiway A, stopped at the sign. If you keep going straight, which taxiway will you be on?
options: A
E
F
None; you must turn left or right
final_quiz.why: The black sign with a yellow A says you are on A [[33:165|AIM 2-3-9a1]]. Left turns are listed to its left; straight ahead and right turns are listed to its right [[33:167|AIM 2-3-10e]]. "F" with an up arrow means straight ahead is Taxiway F [[19:65|AC 150/5340-18H Fig 1-14]].

final_quiz.q: Your radio quits right after you land at a towered airport. While you are still on the runway, the tower shows you a flashing red light. What should you do?
options: Stop right where you are
Taxi clear of the runway in use
Return to your starting point on the airport
Take off again
final_quiz.why: To an aircraft on the ground, flashing red means taxi clear of the runway in use. Steady red means stop, and flashing white means return to starting point [[1:359|PHAK 14-25]].

final_quiz.q: Ground says: "Hold short of Taxiway Echo." Which marking shows where you stop?
options: A single dashed yellow line across the taxiway
Four yellow lines, two solid and two dashed
Yellow dashes on both sides of the centerline
A double dashed yellow line along the taxiway edge
final_quiz.why: A taxiway/taxiway holding position is a single dashed yellow line across the taxiway. Stop so no part of the airplane is past it [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5c]] [[33:152|AIM 2-3-5c]]. The four-line marking is for runways [[33:151|AIM 2-3-5a]].

final_quiz.q: You are taxiing north (heading 360). The wind is from 210 degrees at 15 knots. How should you hold the yoke?
options: Turned left, elevator neutral
Turned right, elevator neutral
Turned left and pushed forward
Turned right and pushed forward
final_quiz.why: Heading north, a wind from 210 comes from your left rear: a quartering tailwind. Hold the upwind (left) aileron down and the elevator down, so the yoke is turned right and pushed forward [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

final_quiz.q: At a nontowered airport, the wind tee points one way but the wind sock shows the wind from a different direction. Which should you trust for the wind?
options: The wind tee, because it is bigger
The wind sock, because a wind tee can be set by hand to the runway in use
Neither; use only the wind reported on CTAF
The wind tee, because it always swings with the wind
final_quiz.why: A wind tee or tetrahedron can be set by hand to line up with the runway in use, so look at the wind sock for the wind [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]]. Check the indicators even when CTAF gives a wind, because that may not be accurate [[1:354|PHAK 14-20]].

final_quiz.q: Tower says: "Cessna 4GW, Runway 18, line up and wait." Which exterior lights should be on as you taxi onto the runway?
options: Only the rotating beacon
Landing lights only
All lights except the landing lights
All lights, including landing lights
final_quiz.why: When entering the departure runway or lining up and waiting, turn on all lights except the landing lights. Landing lights go on when you get the takeoff clearance [[33:266|AIM 4-3-24g]] [[7:10|AC 91-73B 7h(2)(d), (f)]].

final_quiz.q: You start rolling out of your parking spot, close the throttle and test the brakes. The right brake barely slows the airplane. What should you do?
options: Keep taxiing and steer with the left brake
Shut down the engine right away
Add power and test the brakes again at a higher speed
Tell ground and continue to the run-up area
final_quiz.why: Test the brakes as soon as the airplane starts moving. If braking is unsatisfactory, shut down the engine immediately [[24:56|AFH 2-19]].

final_quiz.q: Thick fog has made the visibility very low at your towered airport. In these low-visibility conditions, when should you run checklists and program the GPS?
options: Only when stopped with the brakes set
While taxiing, to save time
While crossing a runway, when ground is quiet
Right after the taxi clearance, while you start to roll
final_quiz.why: In low visibility, give your full attention to taxiing while moving. Hold checklists and nonessential talk until you are stopped with the brakes set [[33:262|AIM 4-3-19d]] [[7:9|AC 91-73B 7g(4)]].

final_quiz.q: Which pilot is most likely to fall into expectation bias while taxiing?
options: A pilot at a new airport who writes down every clearance
A pilot who flies from the same airport every week and always gets the same taxi route
A pilot who asks for progressive taxi
A student who reads back every hold short instruction word for word
final_quiz.why: Pilots who routinely get the same taxi clearance are more likely to hear the clearance they expect instead of the one ATC gave [[30:46|RMH 6-3]] [[24:56|AFH 2-19]]. Fatigue makes it worse [[30:46|RMH 6-3]].

final_quiz.q: During taxi you check the instruments in a left turn. What should a working turn coordinator show?
options: A left turn, with the ball moving to the right
A left turn, with the ball moving to the left
A right turn, with the ball centered
No turn, because the airplane is on the ground
final_quiz.why: The turn indicator should show the correct direction of turn, with the ball moving toward the outside of the turn [[24:58|AFH 2-21]].
